newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver eye weaker platinum prices.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver eye weaker platinum prices.

text.p: The precious metals were mostly quiet on Tuesday as flagship gold consolidated in the aftermath of recent price upheavals, dealers said.
"The gold market does not have a strong opinion of where it is going. It's pretty nervous and people are trying to be as flat as possible," a dealer said.
Bullion was fixed slightly weaker at $368.25 an ounce, versus $368.80 in the morning and $369.00 on Monday afternoon.

Prices gyrated within a relatively narrow price band, first edging up from lower overnight levels and then drifting back in the afternoon, in part due to European-based liquidation of long positions, dealers said.
The market has been jumpy against a backdrop of sharp falls in recent weeks and a strong but short-lived rally sparked by heavy losses in financial markets last Friday.
But a bearish mood prevailed with gold prices hovering at three-year lows and market expectations pinned on an eventual dip to $360 an ounce.
Analysts say gold is more likely to head lower than recover in the near term, with selling by mining houses seen capping rallies and slack seasonal demand failing to support prices.
Steadily declining platinum prices were also casting a pall on the other precious metals, dealers said.
Platinum has been under steady selling pressure which several dealers said likely originated from one or more speculative funds liquidating long positions.
"There's been reasonable action in platinum and it's still being offered," a dealer said.
"With the year-end coming up people have added up their positions and decided to get out."
Platinum was indicated at $367.50/$368.50 an ounce, down $1.30 from Monday's London close.
By contrast, its sister metal palladium popped up $1.25 to $117.50/$118.50 an ounce.
Silver prices were steady at around $4.80/$4.82 an ounce, up two cents from Monday's close.
